concepts.title: Two moving frontiers
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: editorial illustration preview for the white table-of-contents page of the research essay No Place To Land, landscape 3:2 composition.
Primary request: an elegant blue-ink landscape drawing of TWO MOVING FRONTIERS, grounded in the following argument. A compact human-AI unit can now coordinate wider production than inherited organizations and markets can employ. Technical possibility expands faster than both the discovery of worthwhile uses and the construction of authority, investment, access, and cooperation needed to sustain them. Some benefits remain unimagined; others are understood but inaccessible. Co-invention develops the application and its operating setting, and reusable knowledge makes later applications less costly. Do not portray this as an ignorant engineer needing to learn customer value.
Scene: an oblique aerial map, drawn like an exceptionally crafted architectural landscape engraving on pure white paper. Established operating businesses form a small connected landscape toward the lower left. An irregular inner frontier encompasses sustained operating use. A wider irregular frontier encompasses what the new production capability makes technically reachable. Between the frontiers are BOTH a few recognizable proposed operating sites whose connecting roads or bridges are unfinished AND genuinely uncharted terrain, with incomplete surveying contours fading into white. Do not populate the entire outer territory with ready-made valuable projects.
Subject: Several small co-invention sites within the gap show connections and operating structures being constructed together, some existing structures being rearranged. A tested connection has short branching extensions that can support subsequent sites, expressing reuse. No lone heroic engineer, no passive customers. The illustration should make the process of discovering AND making uses workable feel open, conditional, and ongoing.
Style/medium: refined editorial pen drawing, architectural linework, subtle cross-hatching, delicate contour lines, selective very pale blue wash; intellectually serious and evocative, not a slide diagram, dashboard, infographic or quantified data plot.
Palette: restrained C89-like cobalt and navy blue on a pure white background. No black rectangle, no dark sky, no neon glow.
Composition: wide, readable as one integrated landscape, enough simplicity to work at 170 mm width, clear hierarchy and generous white margins; all marks fade naturally to white at the edges, no enclosing border.
Text: ONLY two small, unobtrusive labels, exact wording: "CAPABILITY FRONTIER" by the outer irregular edge and "SUSTAINED USE" by the inner irregular edge. No other text.
Avoid: three labeled input boxes, a box called customer value, flowchart arrows, Venn diagrams, isolated engineer looking for a job, inevitable progress, labels such as growth or success, literal robots, fantasy spacecraft, generic business icons, elaborate dense city panoramas, watermarks, logos.

concepts.title: Landing places built for the earlier producer
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: second editorial illustration preview for the white table-of-contents page of the research essay No Place To Land, landscape 3:2 composition.
Primary request: LANDING PLACES BUILT FOR THE EARLIER PRODUCER. An architectural visual metaphor, exceptionally refined blue-ink editorial line drawing on pure white paper. A new compact human-AI production unit can hold design, implementation, verification and operation together; the available organizational assignments and buying categories still commission those contributions separately. The missing setting is constructed through organizational recomposition and co-invention. The useful offering and the conditions supporting it may need to be developed together; a benefit can also already be understood but impossible to commission. Do not frame the problem as an engineer lacking business sense, customer understanding, or something to do.
Scene: an oblique architectural view across a small gap. On the left, a coherent compact production workshop or architectural unit with interconnected workstations and one accountable human operator, clearly ONE integrated working enclosure spanning a broad scope. This is a functioning production unit, not a lonely job seeker, robot or spaceship. On the right, an established organizational building or structure has four narrow separate landing bays or entrances, each leading into its own divided compartment. Those bays accept separate contributions rather than the coherent scope of the left-hand unit. A few fine connections can reach individual bays but they do not establish a workable home for the integrated responsibility.
Crucial foreground: a new, broader operating landing place is visibly being developed beside and partly within the established structure. Parts of existing partitions are being regrouped; multiple people from the production and business sides work around the same evolving construction. Scaffolding, survey lines, incomplete connections and several faint provisional outlines convey that its purpose, boundary and operating commitments remain under development. It is not a finished perfect socket predetermined to fit the producer, nor a guaranteed valuable result. The established organization is potentially part of the solution, not simply an obstacle. Show meaningful reorganization and shared construction, not just a missing physical bridge.
Style/medium: sophisticated architectural pen engraving, thin cobalt/navy lines, restrained cross-hatching and very pale blue shading; striking integrated editorial composition, enough simplification to remain readable at 170 mm width. Architectural imagination rather than a literal factory or cartoon.
Background/composition: pure white, generous white margins, illustration fades naturally into white at every edge; wide landscape, no frame or border, no dark background.
Text: only these small editorial labels, exact wording: "INTEGRATED SCOPE" near the left working unit; "SEPARATE ASSIGNMENTS" above the old compartmented structure; "DESIGN", "IMPLEMENTATION", "VERIFICATION", "OPERATION" unobtrusively beside the corresponding four old bays. Leave the new construction unlabeled.
Avoid: customer value as a known input box, customer value as a ready-made destination, three-block flowcharts, literal spacecraft or aircraft, sci-fi landing-pad graphics, jigsaw puzzles, engineer with a resume, heroic savior, passive customers, corporate clipart, dark sky, neon glow, watermarks, logos, motivational slogans.
